still_not_described.why: A kill (SIGKILL, power loss, a terminated host) runs no Python handler, so no per-key report can print. What the mode does instead: it printed REMINT-BEGIN and the WILL-WRITE lines before the first put, so an operator with only the log knows the exact keys to inspect, and the capture holds the version each key had before the run. The report of an interruption the process CAN see (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit not caught inside, any BaseException) is described and tested. F8 is marked described=true for that reading only.

not_established: Behaviour against the real bucket: no AWS call was made, the mode was run only against the faked, versioned bucket. That the real bucket is versioned, that HEAD returns VersionId there, and that a HEAD immediately after a put always shows the new version (read-after-write) were not exercised; the state is only as true as that read.
A hard kill (SIGKILL, power loss, an OS signal that cannot be handled), or a kill DURING a put: no handler runs; only the WILL-WRITE lines and the capture remain. Not testable here.

A second writer to the table during the run: the capture is checked against the served heads once before the writes; the report compares each key with the CAPTURE, so a key written by something else after the check would read WRITTEN. Not detected, not tested.

The method-row manifest comparison is against the row the producer returned plus served_thresholds(thresholds) serialised with default=str, as emit_method_row writes it at this commit; if the producer changes how it serialises that manifest, the comparison refuses until the mode is updated (a refusal, not a silent pass).
A head that succeeds but returns a stale version (eventual consistency) would read NOT-WRITTEN for a key that did land; S3 is strongly read-after-write consistent today, which was not re-measured.
Local leftovers after an interruption (stream_parquet temp files under the system temp directory).
The order in which a person restores the keys of a half pair; the restore itself passes through states in which a pair is half. Not examined.
No producer edit was needed; the producer's emit_day and emit_method_row were not changed and nothing was requested of them.
